data.name: Zenessa
data.gender_notes: Zenessa is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: God's Gracious Gift, Derived from Zenobia Meaning 'Living, or Life' and Enna Meaning 'Grace or Favor'. The name Zenessa carries the meaning “God's Gracious Gift” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English. Parents who choose Zenessa usually hope their child will grow to embody god's gracious gift and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A Name for a Child Whose Parents Believe Will Be Blessed with Wisdom and Calmness, and Will Grow up to be a Spiritually Enlightened Individual
data.etymology: Zenessa belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's Gracious Gift.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Zenessa total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Zenessa carries the essence of wisdom and grace, derived from the Zen Buddhist tradition and the biblical name Elisabeth. It serves as a reminder to embrace the inner peace and understanding that comes with maturity and enlightenment.

historical_references.reference: Zenessa of Caesarea was a Syrian Christian saint and martyr who lived in the late 3rd or early 4th century. She is said to have been a virgin and a healer, whose miracles were attested by Saint Eusebius of Caesarea.

According to the Syriac Acts of Zenobius and Zenessa, the two saints were martyred during the reign of Emperor Julian the Apostate (361-363 AD). They were arrested for their Christian faith, and after being subjected to various tortures, were beheaded in Caesarea Maritima in Palestine.
historical_references.time_period: Reign of Emperor Julian the Apostate (361-363 AD)
